target.title: fix(discord): skip malformed legacy thread-bindings store in doctor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readLegacyThreadBindingsStore` in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/model-picker-preferences-migrations.ts` parsed the legacy `state/discord/thread-bindings.json` with an unguarded `JSON.parse`. A partially-written or syntax-broken file (editor save, OOM kill, truncation) threw a raw `SyntaxError` out of the plan's `readEntries`, which runs during `openclaw doctor --fix` via the bundled-channel state-migration loop. One corrupted file killed the whole migration pass with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ...` and no actionable hint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sibling `readLegacyStore` in the same file (5 lines above) already guards its `JSON.parse` with a try/catch that returns `null`. `readLegacyThreadBindingsStore` was the inconsistent outlier — same kind of legacy JSON file, no guard. This makes the two consistent and keeps doctor running when one legacy store is corrupted.

## User Impact

A user upgrading from pre-SQLite state storage with a corrupted `thread-bindings.json` no longer has `openclaw doctor --fix` die with an opaque `SyntaxError`; the malformed store is skipped (its plan yields no entries) and the rest of the migration pass proceeds. Well-formed stores are unchanged; the version-mismatch check is preserved.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A malformed legacy `thread-bindings.json` threw a raw `SyntaxError` out of the plan's `readEntries`, killing the whole `openclaw doctor --fix` migration pass.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `6f0dfa67bd` on branch `fix/discord-doctor-thread-bindings-jsonparse`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-discord-doctor-threadbindings.mjs` — imports the real `detectDiscordLegacyStateMigrations`, writes a real malformed `thread-bindings.json` to a real temp state dir, runs the real detector, and calls the plan's real `readEntries`. No mocks: real fs, real detector, real readEntries.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-discord-doctor-threadbindings.mjs
  wrote malformed store: "{ \"version\": 1, \"bindings\": { , }"
  raw JSON.parse -> SyntaxError (what doctor used to crash on)

  detectDiscordLegacyStateMigrations returned 1 plan(s) (did not throw)
  plan.readEntries returned: [] (skipped malformed store, no crash)

  Verdict: doctor readEntries survives a malformed thread-bindings.json (returns []) instead of crashing
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Over a real malformed `thread-bindings.json`, the detector returns its plan without throwing, and the plan's `readEntries` returns `[]` instead of throwing a `SyntaxError` — so the bundled-channel migration loop can keep going. A raw `JSON.parse` of the same body still throws `SyntaxError` (shown for contrast: that is what doctor used to crash on).
- **What was not tested:** A real upgrade from a pre-SQLite install on a production machine (the temp state dir + real detector is the faithful unit; live `openclaw doctor --fix` against a user vault is the same code path).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/model-picker-preferences-migrations.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Added `skips a malformed legacy thread bindings store instead of crashing doctor`: writes a malformed `thread-bindings.json`, runs the real detector, and asserts the plan's `readEntries` returns `[]` instead of throwing.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended, bounded) - a corrupted legacy `thread-bindings.json` is now skipped instead of killing `openclaw doctor --fix`; well-formed stores and the happy path unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched; only the legacy-file read path.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - only error handling around an existing JSON.parse of a local legacy file.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) - internal to the Discord plugin doctor migration; the detector's plan shape is unchanged.
- Highest-risk area: silently skipping a corrupted store means its thread bindings are not migrated - but the alternative (crash) is strictly worse, and the file is left in place for the user to repair/re-import.
- Mitigation: 8 model-picker-preferences-migrations tests (incl. the new malformed-store case) + node runtime verification driving the real detector over a real malformed file.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)
